statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band on an orderly two-way Friday path, while Stress stays elevated on a multi-decade-high long end and an unresolved Middle East energy sequence.
recommendation: Tail sits below the WATCH threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow danger window covers the final cash half-hour through the 21:00 UTC weekly futures settlement; the remainder of the published window is a weekend halt in which no continuous NQ price path exists.
headline: Orderly two-way Nasdaq-100 close into a weekend halt, with elevated Stress from a 5.18% long end and the unresolved Hormuz sequence
body: NQ futures trade near 30,894 (+0.41%) inside a 30,679-30,997 session range, and the NDX cash index sits around 30,597 (+0.39%) after rejecting both its 30,413.59 low and its 30,667.56 high. Neither extreme is being held and retracements are printing, so the persistent no-retracement structure that defines Tail is absent; VIX at 14.94 (-4.66%) corroborates an orderly path. The macro backdrop is nonetheless genuinely difficult. The US 10-year yield is near 5.18% after a sixth consecutive weekly rise, with the 30-year around 5.47% and an intraday peak of 5.501% reported as the highest since June 2004; reporting cites resilient data, energy-driven inflation, heavy AI-related corporate issuance and hawkish Fed commentary, with traders pricing roughly a 70% chance of a further quarter-point increase at the October meeting. WTI eased 2.17% to 92.56 (Brent near 105) after Iran's foreign minister proposed a conditional seven-day sequence to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, contingent on a full ceasefire, lifting of the naval blockade and oil-sanction waivers, and release of frozen assets. Today's US data was mixed but not destabilising: August durable goods orders came in at 0.0% against a -0.4% consensus, while the final September Michigan sentiment reading of 48.1 remained historically weak with five-year inflation expectations at 3.4%. Shared Finviz context was partial this cycle, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable; the available latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings are internally mixed (Technology +0.85% against Communication Services -0.57%; MSFT +3.7% against META -3.31%) and are treated as non-real-time supporting context only. That combination keeps Stress elevated and Tail low. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekly settlement halts continuous price discovery for the remainder of the published window, so the forecast path describes a dormant market with decaying evidence freshness rather than an improving regime.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Tail stayed inside a 17-22 band and Stress inside 54-59, with the mapped state oscillating between EA_ON and WATCH. The overnight Asian and European hours were the calmest stretch, Tail peaked at 22 during the 09:00 and 11:00 UTC European trend-up phases, and the US session resolved back toward the low band from 15:00 UTC onward as retracements returned. No assessment was published for the 13:00 UTC clock-hour, which is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The near window covers the final US cash half-hour, the 16:00 ET close and the 21:00 UTC CME weekly settlement, after which the published path describes a full weekend halt with no continuous NQ price discovery. Tail steps down to a structural weekend floor and lifts only fractionally late on Saturday as conditional gap proximity to the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen builds. Confidence decays through the halt because live price-path evidence stops refreshing, and Stress stays in the elevated band because the multi-decade-high long end, the unresolved Hormuz conditions and next week's core PCE, ISM and payrolls calendar all remain in force.

forecast.analysis: Observed: NQ futures near 30,894 (+0.4%) after holding a 30,679-30,997 range, NDX around 30,597 off its 30,668 high, VIX down to 14.94. Retracements are occurring and neither extreme is being held, so mean reversion is functioning despite a 5.18% 10-year yield.
